name: Jehoshaphat
charge: Seeking the Lord and walking in his commandments; sending Levites to teach the book of the law through all the cities of Judah; setting the battle in array with singers
summary: He sent princes and Levites round Judah with the book of the law to teach it, and the fear of the Lord fell on the kingdoms round about. When Moab, Ammon and Edom came against him he proclaimed a fast, prayed in the congregation, and put the singers in front of the army. They came to the watchtower and found only dead bodies. His alliances with Ahab's house are their own case.

verses.text: And the Lord was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the first ways of his father David, and sought not unto Baalim;
But sought to the Lord God of his father, and walked in his commandments, and not after the doings of Israel.
Therefore the Lord stablished the kingdom in his hand; and all Judah brought to Jehoshaphat presents; and he had riches and honour in abundance.
And his heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord: moreover he took away the high places and groves out of Judah.
Also in the third year of his reign he sent to his princes, even to Ben–hail, and to Obadiah, and to Zechariah, and to Nethaneel, and to Michaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah.

And with them he sent Levites, even Shemaiah, and Nethaniah, and Zebadiah, and Asahel, and Shemiramoth, and Jehonathan, and Adonijah, and Tobijah, and Tob–adonijah, Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, priests.
And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.
And the fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms of the lands that were round about Judah, so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat.
And Jehoshaphat feared, and set himself to seek the Lord, and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
And Judah gathered themselves together, to ask help of the Lord: even out of all the cities of Judah they came to seek the Lord.
And Jehoshaphat stood in the congregation of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the Lord, before the new court,

And said, O Lord God of our fathers, art not thou God in heaven? and rulest not thou over all the kingdoms of the heathen? and in thine hand is there not power and might, so that none is able to withstand thee?
Art not thou our God, who didst drive out the inhabitants of this land before thy people Israel, and gavest it to the seed of Abraham thy friend for ever?
And they dwelt therein, and have built thee a sanctuary therein for thy name, saying,

If, when evil cometh upon us, as the sword, judgment, or pestilence, or famine, we stand before this house, and in thy presence, (for thy name is in this house,) and cry unto thee in our affliction, then thou wilt hear and help.
And now, behold, the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade, when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned from them, and destroyed them not;
Behold, I say, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of thy possession, which thou hast given us to inherit.
O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.
And all Judah stood before the Lord, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
Then upon Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, came the Spirit of the Lord in the midst of the congregation;

And he said, Hearken ye, all Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, and thou king Jehoshaphat, Thus saith the Lord unto you, Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s.
To morrow go ye down against them: behold, they come up by the cliff of Ziz; and ye shall find them at the end of the brook, before the wilderness of Jeruel.

Ye shall not need to fight in this battle: set yourselves, stand ye still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you, O Judah and Jerusalem: fear not, nor be dismayed; to morrow go out against them: for the Lord will be with you.

And they rose early in the morning, and went forth into the wilderness of Tekoa: and as they went forth, Jehoshaphat stood and said, Hear me, O Judah, and ye inhabitants of Jerusalem; Believe in the Lord your God, so shall ye be established; believe his prophets, so shall ye prosper.

And when he had consulted with the people, he appointed singers unto the Lord, and that should praise the beauty of holiness, as they went out before the army, and to say, Praise the Lord; for his mercy endureth for ever.
And when they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah; and they were smitten.

For the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy them: and when they had made an end of the inhabitants of Seir, every one helped to destroy another.
And when Judah came toward the watch tower in the wilderness, they looked unto the multitude, and, behold, they were dead bodies fallen to the earth, and none escaped.

And when Jehoshaphat and his people came to take away the spoil of them, they found among them in abundance both riches with the dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could carry away: and they were three days in gathering of the spoil, it was so much.
And on the fourth day they assembled themselves in the valley of Berachah; for there they blessed the Lord: therefore the name of the same place was called, The valley of Berachah, unto this day.
Then they returned, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, and Jehoshaphat in the forefront of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for the Lord had made them to rejoice over their enemies.
And they came to Jerusalem with psalteries and harps and trumpets unto the house of the Lord.
And the fear of God was on all the kingdoms of those countries, when they had heard that the Lord fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the realm of Jehoshaphat was quiet: for his God gave him rest round about.
And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:
And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes.
And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

entries.commentary: Jehoshaphat reigned in the place of his father Asa, taking the throne after him. He strengthened himself against Israel, setting himself apart from the northern kingdom's ways. -
He placed forces and garrisons in the fenced cities of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that Asa had taken. A diligent king secures the land and prepares before trouble comes.

The Most High was with Jehoshaphat because he walked in the first ways of his father David and sought not unto Baal. David was a man after the Most High's own heart because he kept the commandments and charged Solomon to keep them.
Jehoshaphat sought the Lord God of his fathers and walked in his commandments, not after the doings of Israel. The way we must walk is defined by the ordinances and laws we are taught. -
Because he obeyed, the Most High established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought presents, and he had riches, honor, and abundance.
His heart was lifted up in the ways of the Lord, not in pride but in devotion. He removed the high places and the groves out of Judah, tearing down false worship.

In the third year of his reign he sent princes and Levites to teach in the cities of Judah, and they carried the book of the Law of the Lord with them. They went throughout all the cities and taught the people, the same pattern we follow, going out into the streets to teach. -
The fear of the Lord fell upon all the kingdoms round about Judah so that they made no war against Jehoshaphat. Teaching the Law had a real effect on the nations; wisdom disarmed his enemies. -
Some of the Philistines brought presents and tribute silver, and the Arabians brought him flocks of rams and he goats. His obedience brought increase even from surrounding peoples.

Jehoshaphat waxed great exceedingly and built castles and cities of store in Judah. Cities of store are cities of provision, like Egypt's storehouses under Joseph in the years of plenty; in captivity our people had neither building nor closet, but the diligent tend to plenty.

He had much business in the cities of Judah, and mighty men of valor were mustered in Jerusalem by the house of their fathers. The captains numbered hundreds of thousands of ready men, prepared for war, waiting on the king beside those set in the fenced cities.

These are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments, commanded to be taught, that thou mightest fear the Lord thy God: the fear always comes up first, thou, and thy son, and thy son's son, all the days of thy life. Hear therefore, O Israel, and observe to do it, that ye may increase mightily. Increase and power are the desire of the people, and keeping the commandments is the one thing our people have not tried; assimilation, the gods of the nations, and politics, liberal or conservative, have all been tried and none of it has worked. The land that floweth with milk and honey is the true riches: cattle, vegetation, agriculture, land to cultivate, the gift that keeps on giving.

Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God is one Lord: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. Thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children: diligently means you do not miss a beat. The children are not to be taught the dance challenges, halloween, and the satanic birthdays, and remember that you teach by your actions, so you fix yourself first. Talk of them when thou sittest in thine house: go through the scriptures at home, the histories of Samson, Joseph, Solomon, and David. When thou walkest by the way: when you run into each other, ask, are you keeping the laws, what four chapters did you read today? When thou liest down, and when thou risest up: the bedtime stories are biblical, the ten plagues of Egypt rather than the fairy tales, prayer before they sleep and when they rise, and even the coloring books painting the images brown, bringing it back to its true course.

Thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thine hand, and they shall be as frontlets between thine eyes: bind them in your mind. The commandments are the light, the torch that guides you and leads you in the correct path. And thou shalt write them upon the posts of thy house, and on thy gates.

When the Lord brings thee into great and goodly cities which thou buildedst not, houses full of all good things which thou filledst not, wells digged which thou diggedst not, and thou shalt have eaten and be full, then beware lest thou forget the Lord which brought thee forth out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and serve him, and shalt swear by his name; ye shall not go after the gods of the people round about you, for the Lord thy God is a jealous God, lest his anger be kindled and destroy thee from off the face of the earth. Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah.

Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes. Testimony is one of the trigger words that confuses our people: the laws are what Moses gave, and the testimonies are the history of the forefathers and foremothers, what they went through and how it was handled according to the laws. Everything correlates: when king David had Uriah killed, that goes back to thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not covet, and bearing false witness; he was dealing with much sin in that one matter. That is how you go precept upon precept, line upon line, to the law and to the testimony. A personal testimony that cannot come back to the Bible is not biblical; if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light, no truth, in them. Thou shalt do that which is right and good in the sight of the Lord: not by personal standards of what feels good in the heart, but by the standard set before us, for the scripture says plainly that the law is good. The reward is to go in and possess the good land, the real wealth, not the bags and rings and sneakers, which are vanity.

When thy son asketh thee in time to come, saying, what mean the testimonies, and the statutes, and the judgments? The children will ask why David did what he did, why Samson, why Miriam was judged, why Moses was barred; the answer starts with the history. Then thou shalt say unto thy son, we were Pharaoh's bondmen in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand, and shewed signs and wonders upon Egypt and upon Pharaoh; he brought us out that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he sware unto our fathers. The Most High always keeps his covenant; he is not a man, that he should lie. The Lord commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive: the fear again stands first, and the commandments are for Israel's good and preservation, obligated and not optional, with punishment for breaking and reward for keeping. And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments: keeping the commandments is what makes you righteous, and righteousness is kept at all times, the fringes worn seven days a week and not on the sabbath only. Words like testimony, righteousness, grace, and faith must be defined out of the scripture itself: the Bible is a dictionary within itself. Egypt means slavery, righteousness means keeping the laws, and going by the Bible's own definitions destroys the private interpretations of the religions.
